scope: One deliberately constructed public resource-lease cleanup case; not a broad detection benchmark.

provenance.selection: Whitelisted experiment, observations, patch and numeric model usage from the recorded public-fixture report. Credentials, model response IDs, raw context, account identifiers and unrelated events are excluded.

experiment.hypothesis: runWithLease leaks the acquired pool lease when the provided task rejects/throws because release() is only called after awaiting task(), so the rejection bypasses cleanup.
experiment.trigger: Call runWithLease(pool, async () => { throw new Error('boom'); }) and observe both that the promise rejects with the same error and that pool.active returns to 0 after the promise settles.
experiment.expected: The returned promise rejects (propagating the same error) and the pool lease is released before/when the promise settles, observable as pool.active===0 after awaiting the rejection.

oracle.quote: When a task rejects or throws, runWithLease must propagate that same error and release its acquired pool lease before the returned promise settles.

assumptions: The contract in README.md applies to acceptance/catcher-release.mjs runWithLease behavior.
A pool implementation that increments active on acquire() and decrements on release() is a valid observable proxy for 'lease released'.
Checking pool.active after awaiting the rejection is sufficient to detect whether release() ran before settlement.
